title: Utkala identity: warmth, knowledge and living art
description: Proposed name, visual identity, cultural reference discipline and artist collaboration direction.
body:
# Utkala identity: warmth, knowledge and living art

## User direction

The user wants investment in a name, logo, colour scheme and warm artistic assets that give the website a local and traditional flavour. This record preserves the resulting creative proposal; it is not a sourced historical claim or an adopted identity.

## Proposed identity

**Utkala — A living encyclopedia of Odisha.** Keep Odisha in the descriptor, discovery copy and page titles. The proposed logo integrates an open book and a boat, connecting knowledge and discovery with the project's maritime editorial theme. The mark is contemporary, not a historical emblem.

Palette: deep red `#8F2435`, warm ivory `#F5EBDD`, charcoal `#24211F`, ochre `#C9923E` and lagoon teal `#245C59`. This is art direction; no single historically definitive Odisha colour is established. Use dark readable text on quiet ivory surfaces, with illustration around story openings rather than behind statistics or paragraphs.

## Cultural references and boundaries

Reuse the saved records on [Raghurajpur and Pattachitra](../culture/raghurajpur-pattachitra.md), [Pipili appliqué](../culture/pipili-applique.md), [Sambalpuri Bandha](../handlooms/sambalpuri-bandha.md) and [Boita Bandana](../culture/boita-bandana.md) when preparing specific briefs. This reuse is not fresh independent verification. These traditions should retain their own names, contexts and practitioner credits.

The first images are AI-generated contemporary concepts using the built-in image generator, not artisan-made works, verified depictions of destinations or historical reconstructions. No named human has reviewed them. Avoid claiming that generated cloth, architecture or ornament represents an authenticated traditional design.

## Review and investment priorities

The creative recommendation is Utkala with the Odisha descriptor. Final name selection, name/domain availability, production typography and a resolved vector identity remain open. The raster mark is a concept. A paid collaboration with Odisha artists should bring specific subjects, original artwork and visible artist credit into the finished site. Obtain a bounded quote; no budget, commission or outreach is recorded here.

The workspace deliverables are in `outputs/brand/v1/`: identity board, logo concept, coastal illustration, botanical divider, exact colour tokens, prompt/provenance record and an artist brief. They are included in the project package, not the self-contained knowledge-only bundle. The public site has not been built or published.

See [editorial direction](editorial-direction.md) and [publication readiness](website-readiness.md).

body:
# Utkala · Odisha — a community encyclopedia

The [detailed product requirements](../product/prd.md) now record audiences, scope, acceptance and growth programmes. Its [preserved versions](../product/versions/index.md) retain historical baselines; the initial PRD is a draft, not a claim of formal approval or implementation.

## Mission

Build a public, community-contributed encyclopedia of Odisha’s places, food, people, skills, history and development. Make its strengths vivid and useful enough that visitors, residents, journalists and government researchers return to it and cite it. Adoption is an ambition, not an achieved endorsement.

The working identity remains **Utkala · Odisha**. GitHub owner: **ahimanikya**, supplied by the user. Suggested repository name: `odisha-encyclopedia`; it has not been created or reserved remotely. The current workspace preserves the existing OKF 0.2 concept paths.

## Three connected experiences

**Discover Odisha.** Attractive destination and food pages, short explanations, readable data stories, maps and practical information. Each page helps the reader understand something or decide what to explore next.

**Understand and cite.** A source panel, definitions, period and geography, estimate status, calculation notes, revision history and downloadable records. A citation identifies the page, stable concept ID, version, source and relevant access date. Original sources remain prominent so researchers can inspect them.

**Contribute.** Git users submit reviewed pull requests; GitHub issue forms remain an optional account-based route.[^github-forms] The agreed launch also includes guest text contributions through Firebase Spark and photos sent to the editorial inbox, optionally through a tested free form relay. Editors publish accepted contributions through Git. These routes are planned, not yet deployed. See the [current technical stack](../technology/technical-stack.md) and [architecture diagrams](../technology/architecture.md).

## The editorial promise

Select stories that reveal Odisha’s strengths. Let independent evidence determine the facts. Preserve important comparison bases, uncertainty and corrections. Commercial relationships and funding must be disclosed. Government information is attributed to its issuing body; the encyclopedia does not imply government endorsement.

Positive coverage and rigorous correction support the same goal: a reputation readers can rely on. A genuine correction is welcome even when it makes a headline less flattering. Clearly label local testimony, folklore, interpretation, announcements and measured outcomes.

## One knowledge source, several public forms

Keep sourced knowledge in the existing Markdown and structured-data records. Public pages, charts, search and download views should be generated from those records and their approved presentation content. Avoid maintaining separate copies of the same statistic across posters and pages.

Preserve concept-path identity, such as `food/chhena-jhili`. Proposed public routes can follow these IDs once the domain and framework are chosen. Renames require aliases and redirects. A record update should reveal the dependent stories and visuals that need attention.

Publication status is separate from OKF lifecycle status and source-check metadata. A stable research method or a machine-checked source extract is not automatically a publication-approved feature. Build the public website from an explicit approved set; keep research leads and unresolved records out of visitor recommendations until suitable for that use.

## Contribution and release flow

**Propose → supply evidence → automated checks → editorial review → merge → approved release → website.**

Automated checks validate structure, references and calculations. Editors assess source quality, meaning, attribution and publication suitability. Named subject reviewers assess specialist claims when needed. GitHub branch rules can require reviews and successful checks before merge; those controls still need remote configuration.[^github-review-rules]

The local scaffold supplies contribution guidance, issue forms, a pull-request template, code ownership and a checks-only workflow. It does not deploy. Contributor checks use read-only permissions and no publishing credentials. Privileged workflows must not run untrusted contribution code.[^github-workflow-security]

## What makes an entry citable

- Stable concept ID and permanent public URL.
- A concise claim linked to the source passage, table or page where possible.
- Clear geography, dates, units, definitions and comparison basis.
- Separate source-check date, editorial-review date and publication date.
- Named contributor and reviewer only when that work actually happened.
- Revision-specific citation and downloadable data for numeric claims.
- Visible corrections, superseded versions and conflicts of interest.

A copied government number is still attributed government data. A local account is labelled testimony until independently corroborated. Our derived figures retain the inputs and calculation. AI assistance is disclosed in provenance and never substitutes for a human review badge.

## Start with a focused public collection

First prepare a small, complete set of tourism, food and heritage entries from the five seed areas. Pair a few well-supported economic stories with these. Add a contributor guide and a source/citation view from the beginning. The number of pages alone is not a launch criterion.

Then expand district coverage, community and Odia-language contributions, makers, nature, festivals, health/fitness and industry. The [visitor roadmap](../visitor-index/expansion-roadmap.md) and [statistics standard](statistics-storytelling.md) guide the reader experience.

## Adoption and governance

Track useful contributions, correction turnaround, current source checks and external citations. Count journalistic or government references only when a saved public link demonstrates them. Do not treat a social share, page view or government source citation as an institutional endorsement.

The owner appoints topic editors and publishes funding and editorial-responsibility information. Contributors should be credited with their consent. Representation across districts and languages requires deliberate recruitment later; no outreach is authorised by this document.

## Before opening publicly

The [decision register](../technology/decisions.md) records the agreed Astro, GitHub Pages and Firebase Spark design, with AI and paid private backups deferred. Finalise the repository name and visibility, domain, content/code licences and named editorial maintainers. Confirm rights for contributed writing, images and datasets. Configure branch protection and release review. Build the website and publication selection mechanism, then review a coherent pilot collection. The local repository has no remote and the website has not been built or published.

[^github-forms]: [GitHub issue and pull request templates](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/about-issue-and-pull-request-templates)
[^github-review-rules]: [GitHub protected branches](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches)
[^github-workflow-security]: [GitHub Actions secure use](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use)

body:
# Utkala · Odisha: editorial and visual direction

## Current campaign priority

Tourism leads the public campaign, supported by food, handlooms, culture and city experiences. The objective is to build pride, curiosity and demand for Odisha, with broader trade and industry chapters later. Follow the [tourism-first strategy](tourism-first-strategy.md); the user’s future personal business is not the organising premise.

## Brand proposition

**Utkala — A living encyclopedia of Odisha**

**A world of stories, waiting to be shared.**

The name and descriptor are the current [identity proposal](brand-identity.md). The second line is optional campaign copy, not a second brand name.

Use Utkala as the user’s chosen cultural expression and Odisha as the clear contemporary geographic name. Keep Odisha in page titles and search descriptions so audiences can find the work. This is a naming strategy, not a claim that historical territorial boundaries were identical in every period.

## Voice

Warm, specific and visually led. Name the food, the textile, the place and the person. Invite curiosity. Build pride through detail. Let the photograph and a short memorable line open the story; put evidence behind the detail.

Suggested recurring invitations: “Taste Odisha.” “Meet its makers.” “Follow a different road.” “See what is growing.” These are creative proposals, not existing official slogans.

## Palette proposal

| Colour | Hex | Editorial use |
|---|---|---|
| Deep red | #8F2435 | Identity and main accents |
| Warm ivory | #F5EBDD | Background and breathing room |
| Charcoal | #24211F | Text and quiet contrast |
| Ochre | #C9923E | Small highlights and chart accents |
| Lagoon teal | #245C59 | Links, secondary actions and selected data series |

This is an art-direction choice for this project. The KB has not established a single official or historically definitive colour representing all Odisha. Keep photographs true to the individual textile, food or place; do not recolour cultural objects to fit the palette.

## India and international framing

For Indian audiences, test weekend discovery, regional food and meaningful purchases as entry points. For global audiences, test making processes, named landscapes and explained cultural context. Avoid treating either audience as uniform: language, motivation and familiarity should guide later testing.

## Copy discipline

Use a strong supported detail instead of an unverified superlative. “More to discover” is an invitation; “never discovered” erases the people who know a place. A growth story needs a period and measure. A maker story needs a name and credit. A travel story needs current practical information before it becomes a recommendation.

## Presenting numbers

Follow the [statistics presentation standard](statistics-storytelling.md): one clear takeaway, one main number, a useful comparison and a simple visual. Explain what the measure means. Keep periods, units and material qualifications visible, with deeper evidence on demand.

body:
# What the first research edition reveals

The strongest opportunity is to make Odisha specific. A name, a place, a process and a person give a reader something to remember and a reason to explore further. This is an editorial inference from the collected material, not a measured conclusion about public awareness.

## 1. Food can become a destination in its own right

The collection already separates breakfast and everyday dishes, pitha, dairy sweets, leaf cooking and place-linked ingredients. [Pitha](../food/pitha.md) provides a multi-part series rather than one generic food post. [Chhena poda](../food/chhena-poda.md) offers a visually accessible introduction; [Koraput coffee](../food/koraput-coffee.md) and [Kalajeera rice](../food/koraput-kalajeera-rice.md) let the story begin with producers.

For Indian audiences, test familiar entry points such as breakfast, festivals and regional food journeys. For international audiences, explain ingredient and technique in plain language while retaining the Odia name. These are audience hypotheses to test. The evidence does not yet quantify culinary variety, market penetration or awareness.

## 2. Textiles need individual identities

[Kotpad](../handlooms/kotpad.md), [Khandua](../handlooms/khandua.md), [Habaspuri](../handlooms/habaspuri.md) and [Berhampuri Patta](../handlooms/berhampuri-patta.md) deserve separate stories. “Odisha handloom” is the collection name, not a substitute for provenance. A useful product page would show fibre, technique, making place, maker and object-specific care.

The commercial opportunity to investigate is a path from appreciation to a credited maker or traceable seller. No sales-growth or under-marketing estimate has been established. Existing promotion, including tourism material and [Boyanika](../handlooms/boyanika.md), means “never marketed” would be inaccurate.

## 3. Tourism becomes richer when places connect

A monument page is useful; a [coast-and-culture story](../stories/coast-and-culture.md) gives it context. A landscape can lead to a textile and then an ingredient in [Koraput](../stories/koraput.md). [Western Odisha](../stories/western-odisha.md) deserves an editorial chapter of its own. These proposed journeys are content structures; travel time, hosts, seasonality and booking details still need work.

## 4. Recognition should be precise

[Konark](../places/konark.md), [Chilika](../places/chilika.md), [Similipal](../places/similipal.md) and [Mayurbhanj Chhau](../culture/mayurbhanj-chhau.md) connect to different international programmes. Give each its actual recognition, date and scope. Combining them under an invented universal UNESCO badge would weaken the work.

## 5. Growth adds a contemporary chapter

The [economic collection](../economy/index.md) adds industry, fisheries and logistics to the cultural picture. It also retains tourism’s recovery alongside its longer comparison. An attractive campaign can select strong, supported stories while preserving enough context to make the numbers understandable.

## What makes the next edition deeper

The next gains come from local voices, specialist review and original media: a cook demonstrating a variant; a weaver explaining a piece; a guide explaining a landscape; a resident showing a neighbourhood. Those details will turn this research foundation into distinctive features.

body:
# Research gaps and source conflicts

## Priority research queue

| Priority | Work | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Food depth | Attributed recipes and variations for six pitha, four everyday dishes and four place-linked sweets; Odia script and pronunciation reviewed by a fluent editor |
| 1 | Textile depth | Maker-reviewed fibre, technique, motif and care notes for six traditions; consented portraits and documented seller provenance |
| 1 | Tourism usability | Five journeys with realistic travel times, seasonal access, willing hosts, practical services and clear source dates |
| 1 | Economic refresh | Latest survey and revisions; comparable historical GSDP endpoints and source locations; retain complete series |
| 2 | District breadth | Coverage map across all 30 districts, with priority for currently missing southern, western and interior places |
| 2 | City life | Representative resident interviews, transport and neighbourhood data, current venues and comparable cost indicators |
| 2 | Market evidence | Search-interest baselines, destination awareness interviews, textile distribution and sales evidence; define “under-marketed” before measuring it |
| 2 | Crafts and ingredients | Cuttack Tarakasi; additional craft forms; millets, greens, fish preparations and community-specific food traditions using specialist/local sources |
| 3 | Language editions | Odia and Hindi editorial review; internationally understandable descriptions; no automatic transliteration presented as verified |

## Conflict: Deomali elevation

The [destination profile](../places/deomali.md) gives 1,762 m, while the [district overview source](../sources/koraput.md) gives 1,672 m. Retain the supported highest-peak description; hold the numerical elevation until an authoritative topographic source resolves the discrepancy. Neither page’s institutional status alone settles it.

## Conflict: Orissa Ikat registry freshness

The [record](../handlooms/orissa-ikat.md) displays Registered, a validity end of 31 January 2025 and a renewal notice. That combination does not establish the present renewal outcome. Historical certificate date is reusable; current validity needs clarification.

## Excluded assertions

The Similipal UNESCO profile contains suspect area/geographic wording; this edition uses the recognition year only. Tourism pages contain several absolute superlatives and health-related food claims; these have not been adopted. Site access, animal sightings and future festival dates are not inferred from old brochures.

## Comparison controls

Keep mining series from different agencies distinct. Keep current-price export value apart from physical output and real GSVA. Keep tourist visits apart from unique people. The [tourism comparisons](../economy/comparison-09-tourism.md) include the pre-pandemic benchmark as well as [recent recovery](../economy/comparison-10-tourism.md).

## Research backlog is not proof of absence

A missing entry means the project has not researched it sufficiently. It does not mean the tradition or place is unknown, undiscovered or unimportant.

## Maritime trade research

A [dedicated research queue](../history/research-agenda.md) now tracks archaeological chronology, historical place attribution, country-level exports, festival sales and cultural-transmission claims.

## Visitor index: priority additions and conflicts

Complete the [five seed areas](../visitor-index/index.md) with named food vendors, route endpoints and transport modes, current site access, water/toilets, accessibility features and accommodation details. Unknown amenities indicate missing research, not absence. Extend coverage beyond these initial areas.

The [Konark tourism profile](../sources/visitor-konark-conflict.md) contains inconsistent chronology and practical information. Keep UNESCO for the heritage description and do not reuse that profile’s fees, hours or restrictions without resolution. The [IndianOil release](../sources/visitor-konark-amenities.md) is dated 2018 despite a newer page footer. Museum cafe tenders are not evidence of service operation. Tourist-office contact fields contain inconsistencies, so the index retains the source-listed location and official directory link only; addresses still need confirmation.

## Smart cities, rare earths, semiconductors and FDI

The [growth-journey queue](../journeys/research-agenda.md) tracks project outcomes, corridor implementation, investment-scope reconciliation and newer DPIIT releases. The saved FDI series ends in March 2026 and the latest checked SCM city snapshot is 1 March 2026. Do not present them as real-time measures.

## Broader investment coverage

The user replaced the standalone FDI monitor with [domestic and foreign investment](../journeys/investment.md). Establish the meaning of survey-reported implementation, project-level expenditure, domestic/foreign coverage, de-duplication and comparable time series before computing a statewide realised total. Full-survey industrial figures and less precise summary variants are recorded separately.

## Statistical atlas expansion

The [coverage map](../statistics/coverage.md) records source conflicts, indexed-only captures, outdated baselines and domain gaps. Fresh checks found conflicting 2024 foreign-tourism figures; do not reuse that total as an uncontested headline. NFHS-6 includes new Odisha estimates and source-restated NFHS-5 baselines; preserve vintages.

title: How knowledge is recorded and reused
description: How knowledge is recorded and reused — research and reuse notes.
body:
# How knowledge is recorded and reused

## What this collection contains

This bundle follows the published Open Knowledge Format 0.2: concept documents in Markdown with YAML metadata, source references, lifecycle fields and linked indexes.[^okf] The producer’s additional fields describe geography, aliases, evidence status and publication readiness. They are local extensions, not new OKF requirements.

## Three layers

1. **Sourced knowledge:** a narrow factual statement tied to a source, with the source’s scope retained.
2. **Interpretation and creative proposals:** editorial choices, campaign language and suggested connections. These are not measured findings.
3. **Open research:** missing local detail, disagreements, operational checks and questions requiring specialist or participant input.

## Evidence handling

Primary registries support designation claims. Statistical publications support named measures and periods. Institutional tourism pages support destination and cultural descriptions, but promotional assertions still require judgment. A contributor post on a government-hosted site remains a contributor post; a chef interview describes that chef’s account, not every household’s practice.

New cultural records were checked against targeted web page or PDF extracts. Their verification scope is stated in metadata. Some source access consisted of indexed passages, not complete PDFs. Source entries disclose this; the collection does not pretend to contain complete archived originals. Only concise extracted knowledge and bibliographic information are retained.

Earlier economic and city evidence was migrated with its original caveats. It is marked as imported and has no new source-verification event. Recalculating a percentage establishes arithmetic consistency, not source accuracy. No record claims human review.

## Freshness

Review dates are editorial schedules. They do not mean a historical designation expires on that date. Recheck financial releases after the next survey; live travel information before each publication; registry validity before a current GI claim; and historical/cultural records annually or when new evidence appears.

## Reuse

Search locally first. Follow the source and caveat for a proposed claim. If the record answers a stable historical question, reuse the saved nucleus. Browse again when the question is new, the record is stale, sources conflict or a current operational detail is needed. Add the result here so the same research is not repeated.

This edition is a substantial starting collection. It is not a census of Odisha’s foods, communities, textiles or destinations.

[^okf]: [Open Knowledge Format, version 0.2](https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/knowledge-catalog/blob/main/okf/SPEC.md)

title: Making Odisha’s numbers easy to understand
description: A story-led presentation standard for statistics, visitor indexes, posters and videos.
evidence_status: Editorial guidance; numerical examples reuse existing KB records without new source verification.
body:
# Making Odisha’s numbers easy to understand

The user wants statistics to be consumable, meaningful and easy to read. Lead with a memorable takeaway, a clearly labelled number and its relevance to the reader. Keep the research depth available behind the experience.

## The public unit: one small story

1. **Headline:** say what changed or why the detail is interesting.
2. **Hero number:** one main statistic, with its measure and period alongside it.
3. **Meaning:** one sentence explaining what it tells us. Connect it to a person, place or experience only where evidence supports that connection.
4. **Visual:** use the simplest form that makes the point clear: a labelled comparison, a short trend, a map or a credited photograph.
5. **Invitation and evidence:** offer a relevant next step and an expandable source/method panel. Keep any qualification that changes the headline’s meaning visible beside the number.

Aim for a takeaway in three seconds, understanding in thirty seconds, and deeper evidence on demand. These are design targets, not measured audience results. Test actual comprehension with readers later.

## Make the format fit the subject

- **Growth:** one headline and a small chart showing the full relevant period. Label the start and end; show intervening years when available.
- **Food:** a named dish, an appetising credited photograph, its place association and a short reason to try it. Add a serving venue once established.
- **Heritage:** a distinctive detail, a strong image and a clear location. Add visitor information where checked.
- **Facilities:** readable service labels with location and freshness information. Distinguish “listed by the operator” from currently confirmed availability.
- **Regional collections:** a map or a few destination cards with filters. A research entry count is a count of this collection, not Odisha’s total food or heritage inventory.

Default to one main number per card, one story per poster and one main idea per short video. On an opening screen, use at most three supporting facts before inviting the reader to explore. These are project defaults; clarity takes precedence over a rigid count.

## Draft examples from the saved research

These examples demonstrate presentation. They reuse imported source data and checked arithmetic; they have not received a fresh source check or publication review in this update.

### Tourism: a recovery story

**Tourist visits rose 13.1% in 2024**

**1.11 crore visits** · Odisha · calendar year 2024

Up from 97.7 lakh in 2023—about 12.8 lakh additional recorded visits in a year.

**Visible context:** This is a one-year recovery comparison. Visits remained below the 2019 level of 1.54 crore. Counts cover domestic and foreign tourist visits, not unique people.

**Visual direction:** show 2019, 2023 and 2024 as three labelled bars starting at zero. Identify them as selected years; do not draw a continuous annual trend through missing years.

**Next action:** Explore Odisha’s destinations.

**Evidence:** [2023–2024 comparison](../economy/comparison-10-tourism.md) and [2019 benchmark](../economy/comparison-09-tourism.md). For an international edition, display 11.1 million visits instead of 1.11 crore. Exact values remain in the linked records.

### Manufacturing: growth with its basis explained

**Manufacturing’s economic contribution grew 26% over five years**

**26% real growth** · Odisha · FY2019–20 to FY2024–25

The sector added more economic value after adjusting for price changes. This measure does not establish growth in jobs, company sales or investment.

**Visible caption:** Manufacturing gross state value added at constant 2011–12 prices. FY2024–25 is a first revised estimate. Rounded from 26.2%.

**Visual direction:** show all six saved annual observations so the rise, subsequent fall and recovery remain visible. Avoid an arrow implying uninterrupted annual growth.

**Next action:** Explore the manufacturing story.

**Evidence:** [Saved manufacturing series and source](../economy/manufacturing.md).

## Readable numbers and honest visuals

Use lakh and crore for Indian audiences; use million and billion for international audiences. Keep the currency visible and avoid currency conversion unless its date and exchange-rate basis are saved. Round deliberately: one decimal place is usually enough for percentages. Calculate changes from the underlying values before rounding.

Keep calendar years separate from financial years; real growth separate from nominal growth; percentage change separate from percentage-point change; visitors separate from visits; announcements separate from realised outcomes. Rankings need the ranked group, measure and year beside them.

Use direct labels, readable text and strong contrast. Avoid 3D charts, decorative gauges, crowded legends and colour-only meanings. Bar charts begin at zero. Explain a restricted line-chart scale when used. Do not hide a material benchmark or estimate status in a source drawer.

Sources, exact values, calculation notes and fuller tables belong in the evidence view, with downloadable data available for readers who want it. Public pages should answer a reader’s question before presenting additional detail.

## Keep curiosity connected to action

A tourism statistic can introduce an exploration page. A food story can lead to a confirmed maker or venue. A textile story can lead to a credited artisan and purchase route. A production statistic can lead to a sourced industry profile. Do not infer job creation, tourist spending or local income from a different measure.

Measure whether readers understand and remember the takeaway, then whether they save, share, explore or enquire. Positive audience response is a research question until observed.

title: Tourism first: build attention, pride and demand for Odisha
description: Current user direction, audience objectives, a twelve-piece pilot proposal and a later podcast pathway.
instruction_basis: User direction in this conversation, 2026-09-27; implementation choices are proposals.
body:
# Tourism first: build attention, pride and demand for Odisha

## Purpose and order

Build a compelling public reputation for Odisha that motivates people within the state and draws interest from India and the wider world. Tourism is the first practical focus. Food, handlooms, culture, landscape and city experiences supply the opening stories. Better trade and business opportunities are the longer-term objective.

The user’s eventual personal venture does not determine the campaign. Health and fitness, mineral processing and other industries are possible later chapters. A podcast is a possible later format, not a production commitment or a prerequisite for starting.

This direction reflects the user’s instruction of 27 September 2026. It takes priority over earlier suggestions that put an economic overview or a maritime trade campaign at the centre of the first release. Those remain useful supporting collections.

## What the audience should take away

| Audience | Intended response | Useful next action |
|---|---|---|
| People in Odisha, including the diaspora | Pride, possibility and recognition of specific local strengths | Share a story, contribute knowledge, nominate a maker or host |
| People elsewhere in India | Curiosity and a concrete reason to explore Odisha | Save a journey, read a food feature, enquire about a visit |
| International audiences | A clear, memorable introduction to places and people | Explore an explained itinerary, meet a maker, seek a relevant connection |

These are campaign objectives. Audience response and business impact have not yet been measured.

## Editorial promise

**Utkala · Odisha — more to discover, more to share.**

Make Odisha desirable through specific experiences. Let readers see what they could taste, learn, wear, explore or participate in. Use economic achievements when they reinforce confidence in contemporary Odisha. The maritime identity can give a feature depth without requiring every tourism story to become a trade-history lesson.

## First pilot: six stories, two formats each

Develop a short video treatment and a saveable poster or carousel for each selected story. This proposed twelve-piece pilot is a manageable learning batch, not a scheduled publishing commitment. Selection depends on available media, verified details and willing contributors.

| Creative opening | Research anchor | What the feature must deliver |
|---|---|---|
| Your next journey could begin with a dish | [Pitha collection](../food/pitha.md) | Distinct named preparations, credited cook and verified recipe context |
| Follow the coast. Stay for the stories. | [Coast and culture](../stories/coast-and-culture.md) | A coherent invitation connecting place, food and making; logistics before itinerary claims |
| Meet the hands behind the cloth | [Woven Odisha](../stories/woven-odisha.md) | A named maker, a specific textile and a traceable next step |
| A landscape you can taste | [Koraput](../stories/koraput.md) | Locally grounded links among landscape, ingredients and makers |
| Follow the thread west | [Western Odisha](../stories/western-odisha.md) | A distinct regional perspective with local contributors |
| Meet the city with someone who calls it home | [Bhubaneswar](../cities/bhubaneswar.md) and [Cuttack](../cities/cuttack.md) | A resident-led experience with current, checked visitor details |

All opening lines above are creative proposals. They are not rankings, counts of all available experiences or claims of measured audience demand.

## A shareable data point needs a story

For each candidate, save four things: the exact supported claim, its source and date, the visual that explains it, and why someone would pass it on. A recognition, a specific technique or a surprising place connection can be as useful as a large number.

Use this compact content structure:

1. **Opening:** one memorable idea that is understandable without prior knowledge of Odisha.
2. **Proof:** a sourced detail, dated number, documented process or attributed voice.
3. **Experience:** show what the reader could see, taste, learn or do.
4. **Invitation:** one relevant next step, such as saving, sharing, discovering a maker or planning a visit.

Do not force an impressive-looking number into every piece. Counts of dishes in our selection are not counts of Odisha’s entire cuisine. An old city ranking is not a current universal liveability verdict. Keep essential qualifications in the visible caption.

## How to learn what spreads

Treat virality as a result to observe. Test alternative openings while keeping the underlying claim fixed. Compare similar formats and reporting windows, and record whether reach was organic or paid.

Track three layers separately: attention (reach, completion and shares per reach); interest (saves, meaningful replies and visits to fuller stories); and action (qualified tourism enquiries, maker referrals and attributable bookings or purchases). A popular post does not by itself establish increased tourism or economic impact. Establish a baseline before drawing growth conclusions.

Preserve useful audience questions and contributor suggestions in the KB, with consent where personal material is involved. Those questions can shape the next research and production batch.

## Website and podcast sequence

The first website should help visitors discover and act: Explore, Taste, Woven & Made, and Stories, supported by a readable source layer. City life can sit inside journeys initially. Growth and maritime research remain available for deeper features and later expansion.

A podcast can grow from subjects that repeatedly attract substantive interest and guests with firsthand knowledge. Possible guest roles include a cook, weaver, guide, tourism operator, cultural researcher and founder. Each conversation should reveal a place or practice, examine an opportunity and offer a useful next step. Short extracts can feed the same story collection.

Before commissioning a season, establish the editorial theme, available guests and an achievable production rhythm. No guest outreach, recording, AI-clone production or publishing is authorised merely by this planning document.

## What happens next in the work

Prioritise the six pilot research anchors, identify the best available visual and contributor for each, and complete only the factual gaps needed for those stories. Maintain the broader KB so later health, fitness and industry work can build on it. Make the first public experience feel like an invitation to Odisha.

## Current build priority

The user’s next priority is the [linked food, heritage and facilities index](../visitor-index/index.md). Deepen usable destination pages, then progressively add the other [discovery indexes](../visitor-index/expansion-roadmap.md). Specific, supported experiences should build pride and interest in Odisha.

title: Website plan and publication readiness
description: Website plan and publication readiness — research and reuse notes.
body:
# Website plan and publication readiness

There is enough material to define the website’s identity and build its editorial structure. A polished public launch still needs original or licensed media, local review and practical information for the journeys it recommends.

## Current technology plan

The [technology collection](../technology/index.md) records the user-agreed launch architecture and [growth roadmap](../technology/growth-roadmap.md). Use Astro/TypeScript and GitHub Pages, with Git-maintained read-only knowledge and Firebase Spark for private dynamic text. Receive photos through email or a tested free relay; publish approved copies manually through Git. AI chat, Blaze and paid private backups are deferred. These choices supersede earlier unspecified-host and account-free-intake-later proposals; implementation remains pending.

## Tourism-first release

The [current campaign direction](tourism-first-strategy.md) puts tourism first. Organise the opening experience around **Explore, Taste, Woven & Made, and Stories**, with visible supporting sources. Feature city life through practical journeys and residents’ voices. Maintain growth and maritime knowledge for selected deeper features and later expansion.

Begin with the strongest completed pilot stories rather than requiring a fixed number of pages in every sector. Each feature needs an inviting opening, credited visuals, a specific supported detail and a useful next action. Tourism recommendations need current logistics; maker referrals need traceable attribution and availability.

The immediate objective is interest in Odisha that can develop into visits and commercial relationships. A podcast is a later editorial extension. Health, fitness and mineral-processing opportunities are later chapters, with their own research requirements. No personal venture is assumed.

## Readiness today

| Component | State |
|---|---|
| Content architecture and editorial direction | Drafted |
| Name, palette, logo and illustration direction | First AI-generated concept kit prepared; production identity and local artist collaboration pending |
| Sourced food, textile, destination and culture nuclei | Available in this KB |
| Existing economic/city evidence and growth calculations | Preserved; calculation checks provided |
| Complete food recipes and Odia-language review | Pending |
| Maker interviews, credited portraits and verified purchase routes | Pending |
| Licensed photography and video library | Pending |
| Current travel logistics and operating information | Pending |
| User’s AI-clone service and production access | Not established in this task |

## Publishing workflow

Select a concept, complete its open research, develop the feature, confirm media rights and participant attribution, check changing facts, then record the final review. Keep the durable knowledge here even if the public copy is shorter. Each public feature should carry its KB concept IDs internally so a source update can identify affected pages.

No public website has been built or published as part of this research edition.

The user has since authorised weekly autonomous updates to the Git repository and website. The [weekly agent](../methods/weekly-data-agent.md) is active for local source monitoring and validated KB updates. Remote publication remains pending the actual GitHub connection, initial project onboarding and website deployment; this is a setup gap, not a recurring approval requirement.

## Maritime layer

Add an optional “Trade & the World” collection using the [evidence map](../history/maritime-evidence.md) and [qualified linked data](../methods/maritime-linked-data.md). Historical and contemporary layers should remain visually distinct. Each edge needs a source reveal; no diagram should imply continuous routes or causation where only an editorial pairing exists.

## Linked visitor indexes

The [visitor index](../visitor-index/index.md) now connects five areas to food, heritage and facility records. Use it for Explore, Taste and Plan your visit. Facility listings are a research seed: current operating checks, named food providers, routes and credited media remain launch requirements. The indexes are directories, not scored state rankings.

## Reader-facing statistics

Use [small, meaningful data stories](statistics-storytelling.md) throughout the website. Present visitor indexes as browsable destination, food and service cards. Keep detailed research tables in an optional evidence view. User comprehension and usefulness guide the design; large data grids are not the default public experience.

## Community encyclopedia direction

The user now wants a public, Git-backed encyclopedia with contributions through GitHub, intended owner `ahimanikya`. The [community model](community-encyclopedia.md) adds contributor review, versioned citations, corrections and explicit publication selection. The local GitHub templates and checks are prepared; the public site, remote settings and release pipeline remain to be implemented. Journalistic and government reference use is an aspiration to measure through actual citations.

## Growth-journey collection

Add four optional story entrances: [Smart cities](../journeys/smart-cities.md), [Rare earths](../journeys/rare-earths.md), [Semiconductors](../journeys/semiconductors.md) and [Investment in Odisha](../journeys/investment.md). Use one lead statistic and a dated timeline or simple chart; retain evidence-state labels. These extend the encyclopedia while tourism remains the first public focus.

## Statistical atlas

A broad [source-linked atlas](../statistics/index.md) now supports concise topic stories and a district banking layer. Source conflicts and indexed-only captures are marked for further review. Research depth does not automatically make every observation ready for a public headline.

# Bhubaneswar: city life with cultural depth

Bhubaneswar’s initial research file combines city indicators with cultural experiences. The stored [Ease of Living rank](../evidence/u01.md) belongs to the 2020 edition and its population category. The [Swachh Survekshan result](../evidence/u04.md) belongs to the 2024–25 edition. Neither establishes a current all-purpose “best city” claim.

## Marketing opportunity

Create a resident-hosted day: breakfast, an Old Town encounter, a craft or museum visit, and an evening chosen by an actual resident. [Korakhai](../food/korakhai.md) provides one specific food connection. [The existing visitor-experience record](../evidence/u12.md) offers starting points for further research.

## Planning and infrastructure

The [BDA town-planning mechanism](../evidence/u07.md) documents land pooling and plot readjustment. [Declarations of intention](../evidence/u08.md) are planning stages, not completed infrastructure. The [Gujarat comparator](../evidence/u10.md) prevents a misleading claim of national uniqueness.

## Research still needed

Collect neighbourhood-level transport, current public spaces, representative rents, university and workplace locations, resident interviews, venue choices and measured air-quality data. The research has not established comparative nightlife quality, broad affordability, a youth-friendliness rank or consistently low pollution. Use named experiences until those comparisons exist.

title: Odisha’s GDP story: scale, momentum and meaning
description: Odisha’s GDP story: scale, momentum and meaning — research and reuse notes.
body:
# Odisha’s GDP story: scale, momentum and meaning

The most useful economic narrative connects the size of the economy to visible sectors and places. Lead with a clear, dated number and then show what it represents.

## Opening evidence

The preserved survey records give **₹9.88 lakh crore nominal GSDP** and **7.9% real GSDP growth** for FY2025–26, both advance estimates. These are two different measures: [economic size](../evidence/e02.md) and [inflation-adjusted annual growth](../evidence/e01.md). They can sit side by side if labelled properly.

## Suggested message

“Odisha’s next chapter is taking shape.” Follow it with the economic-size number, its estimate label, and a sequence covering ports, production, food, services and people. Treat the phrase as campaign language rather than a statistical finding.

## A richer proof sequence

Use [construction’s five-year real growth](construction.md), [fisheries production](comparison-01-fisheries.md) and [Paradip cargo](comparison-05-port-logistics.md) as distinct stories. Their measures must stay separate: economic value added, physical output and port throughput. They cannot be added into a single “growth” total.

The [industry growth collection](index.md) retains complete six-year sector series so the campaign can use both the positive endpoint comparison and a truthful chart. A changing trajectory is more informative than an invented uninterrupted boom.

## Publication controls

Use a common vintage and price basis for any India comparison. The state survey’s national comparator and later national estimates are not automatically comparable: see [survey comparator](../evidence/e04.md) and [later national estimate](../evidence/e05.md). Do not call nominal expansion real growth. Do not turn per-capita income into a claim about every household. Announced investments and jobs remain announcements until completion is established.

The nominal ten-year tripling angle from earlier work needs its historical starting value added as an independently locatable record before it becomes a website headline.

## Fresh series expansion

The [economic-size and income atlas](../statistics/economic-size-and-income.md) records the current-price 2018–19 to 2025–26 series with revision/advance-estimate labels and explicit lakh-to-crore conversion. It supports the saved five-year nominal comparison, not a real-growth or ten-year claim.

title: Pitha: a collection, not one dish
description: Pitha: a collection, not one dish — research and reuse notes.
body:
# Pitha: a collection, not one dish

Odisha’s pitha repertoire includes pan-cooked, boiled, baked and fried preparations.[^food-tourism]

For the website, make this a browsable collection. Begin with [chakuli](chakuli.md), [poda](poda-pitha.md), [enduri](enduri-pitha.md), [sijha manda](manda-pitha.md), [kakara](kakara-pitha.md) and [arisa](arisa-pitha.md). These are examples, not an inventory of all Odia pitha.

## Editorial proposal

“How many ways can a home say welcome?” is a stronger opening than a large unverified dish count. Each page should show a whole serving, a texture close-up and the maker’s hands. Let the cook identify the occasion, ingredients and variation. A six-part series can introduce one preparation at a time and end with a tasting spread.

## Recipe research template

Capture local name and approved spelling; place; contributor credit and consent; ingredient quantities; preparation method; household variation; occasion; serving context; photography rights; and dietary/allergen information verified from that recipe. Do not infer that every version of a dish has the same ingredients.

No complete recipe has yet been established in this KB.

[^food-tourism]: [The Taste of Odisha](https://odishatourism.gov.in/content/tourism/en/the-taste-of-odisha.html)

# Bali and Indonesia: three distinct kinds of connection

Ardika and Bellwood’s Sembiran research identifies early Indian contact with Bali.[^maritime-sembiran] Odisha’s official Bali Jatra account commemorates maritime exchange with Southeast Asia, particularly Bali.[^maritime-culture-2025]

## Link carefully

The first supports an archaeological India–Bali connection; the second establishes a contemporary Odisha commemoration. Neither alone proves that every Indian object in Bali came from modern Odisha. The research graph keeps both links without collapsing them into an exclusive origin claim.

## An epigraphic lead

A scholarly discussion references foreign communities including Kling in Javanese inscriptions. This edition records it as a lead: the underlying transcription, dating and geographic interpretation must be checked. The term must not be automatically equated with modern Odia identity.[^maritime-cane-lead]

## Commercial next step

Obtain Odisha-origin exports to Indonesia by product and year, then identify an actual buyer or producer relationship. National India–Indonesia totals cannot fill a state-level data gap.

# Manikapatna: overseas objects and a port site

The 2026 research abstract reports Chinese ceramics and Chinese and Sri Lankan coins at Manikapatna; it describes activity around the sixth–seventh through seventeenth centuries CE.[^maritime-manikapatna-2026]

The 2022 paper reports earlier excavation phases of second century BCE–fifth/sixth century CE and ninth–nineteenth century CE.[^maritime-anchor]

title: Maritime Odisha: the evidence structure
description: Maritime Odisha: the evidence structure — evidence, scope and reuse.
body:
# Maritime Odisha: the evidence structure

Odisha’s maritime story can be connected through objects, sites, commemorations and modern trade observations. Those links support an outward-looking commercial identity. They do not supply an ancient export ledger or a continuous company history.

## The strongest connected stories

| Connection | Historical or cultural anchor | Modern link | Claim boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| China | [Ceramic and coin finds](manikapatna.md), plus [Khalkatapatna](khalkatapatna.md) | [Export destination observation](../trade/export-destinations.md) | Archaeological circulation does not specify a direct sailing route |
| Sri Lanka | Reported coins at [Manikapatna](manikapatna.md) | Odisha-specific current trade value still needed | No invented modern total |
| Indonesia / Bali | [Commemoration](../culture/boita-bandana.md) and [India–Bali archaeological research](bali-and-indonesia.md) | Country-specific state export and buyer data still needed | Indian contact is not automatically Odisha-exclusive |
| Malay Peninsula | [Published route reconstruction](palur-and-bay-routes.md) | Malaysia appears in the export-destination table | Historical region and modern national territory are different |
| Gujarat | [Archaeometric provenance of an anchor](manikapatna-anchor.md) | Potential contemporary coastal-logistics research | Rock provenance is not a complete ship itinerary |
| Enterprise in Odisha | [Boita Bandana](../culture/boita-bandana.md) | [Paradip’s own commemoration](../trade/paradip-bridge.md) and [fair sales reporting](../trade/baliyatra-commerce.md) | Cultural pride is not a measured cause of business performance |

## A chronology with visible uncertainty

Read each site’s dated record separately. The 2022 Manikapatna paper’s archaeological phases and the 2026 conference abstract’s activity window are not identical. Neither should be converted into “uninterrupted global trade for 2,000 years.” Object dates, occupation dates and voyage dates are different variables.

## Geographic discipline

Use Utkala · Odisha as the campaign identity. In historical records, retain the source’s Kalinga, Utkal or Odra terminology and time-dependent geography. Do not assign every port of the wider historical east-coast network to today’s Odisha. Treat cultural transmission as a specific, testable proposition: which practice or object, at which place and date, with what evidence of direction?

## Reusable data

The [linked-data method](../methods/maritime-linked-data.md) explains the entity and claim graph. A missing number is stored as missing, never as zero. The [research queue](research-agenda.md) prioritises the remaining trade and historical joins.

title: Next evidence needed for a global trading story
description: Next evidence needed for a global trading story — evidence, scope and reuse.
body:
# Next evidence needed for a global trading story

## Highest-value joins

1. **Odisha → country → product → year:** obtain official state-of-origin exports at HS product-code level, in both value and quantity, for China, Indonesia, Malaysia, Vietnam and Sri Lanka. Retain state-of-origin methodology, revisions, currencies and complete annual series. This will identify real product relationships rather than relying on country-level symbolism.
2. **Product → producer → buyer:** identify public, attributable commercial examples in metals, seafood, textiles and food. Confirm actual shipments or contracts before treating plans or trade-fair meetings as outcomes.
3. **Festival → seller → sales:** obtain ORMAS and district closing reports, definitions of sales, participating-stall counts and event dates. Separate visitor entries from unique people; avoid economic-impact multipliers without a study.
4. **Object → excavation → origin:** retrieve Manikapatna and Khalkatapatna catalogues, accession identifiers, dating methods and museum locations. Ask a qualified archaeologist to review the proposed public claims.
5. **Inscription → transcription → translation:** pursue the Kling/Cane and related Javanese leads through original editions and current scholarship. Historical ethnonyms need contextual interpretation.
6. **Cultural influence:** investigate one named practice or object at a time with Indonesian and other regional scholarship. Similarity alone does not establish source, direction or exclusive authorship.

## Known issues to preserve

- Manikapatna chronology differs across the 2022 research paper and 2026 abstract.
- The 2019 Roman-contact paper’s discussion is substantially more cautious than its abstract.
- Export destination percentages need underlying-table denominator reconciliation before conversion into rupee values.
- The survey’s marine-destination Figure 4.9 contains an unresolved editorial note about quantity versus value; do not substitute those shares for the overall export-destination table.
- The 2024 fair-sales article has inconsistent title metadata and lacks an audited closing statement.

## Measurement plan

For future campaigns, track qualified enquiries, maker referrals, completed purchases, export leads progressing to confirmed orders and visitor bookings with consented attribution. Set a baseline before launch. Historical content is an entry point; business outcomes need contemporary measurement.

This is a research queue, not evidence that ancient trade volumes, trader counts or market shares are known. The initial maritime module is not an exhaustive archive of all Odisha history.

# Roman connections: why the full paper changes the claim

The 2019 reassessment questions several supposed Roman finds and concludes that direct Odisha–Roman maritime contact lacks tangible support in the evidence reviewed. Indirect exchange remains a possibility.[^maritime-romans-2019]

## Research consequence

Its abstract can sound stronger than its conclusion. Read the discussion on pages 1394–1395 before citing the paper. Do not use “Odisha traded directly with Rome” as an established headline on the basis of this source.

This does not negate Odisha’s wider maritime history. It identifies which particular route claim is unresolved. Keep this record discoverable so future marketing research does not repeatedly pick up the stronger, unsupported version.

## Geographic naming

The paper also distinguishes historical names and changing boundaries. That supports retaining historical geography separately from present-day state identity.

[Maritime overview](maritime-evidence.md)

# Odisha FDI index — recorded inflows and trends

**Current use:** Background reference. The user replaced the standalone FDI focus with [Investment in Odisha](investment.md). The weekly agent no longer monitors this as an independent headline track. The saved numbers were rechecked against DPIIT Table 5 on 27 September 2026; the USD-million units are confirmed.

## The reader’s takeaway

**US$69.72 million of FDI equity inflows recorded in 2025.**

The comparable calendar-year figures were **US$11.83 million in 2023** and **US$4.41 million in 2024**. The 2025 rise was **US$65.31 million**, or approximately **15.8 times** the 2024 amount, from a small base.[^journey-fdi-mar2026]

## Index scope

This is an organised tracker of official **FDI equity inflows**, not a new composite investment-attractiveness score. DPIIT’s state detail covers the equity component; it is not total FDI including reinvested earnings and other capital.[^journey-fdi-mar2026]

## The saved time windows

- **2023:** US$11.83 million.
- **2024:** US$4.41 million.
- **2025:** US$69.72 million.
- **January–March 2026:** US$14.68 million; a partial year.
- **October 2019–March 2026:** reported cumulative US$257.19 million, also reported as ₹2,054.88 crore.[^journey-fdi-mar2026]

All figures above are recorded as assigned to Odisha in the cited DPIIT table. The three full-year observations are calendar years. The table pools October 2019–December 2022 into one US$156.54-million cell; that cell is not an annual observation.

## Meaning and presentation

Show the three complete years as directly labelled bars beginning at zero. Put the 2026 partial-year value on a separate card. Prefer “FDI equity inflows rebounded in 2025” with the absolute values visible. A 15.8× headline alone would overstate the breadth of evidence by concealing the small base.

Use the source’s reported INR and USD values; do not treat their ratio as a current exchange rate. Keep investment summits, domestic project proposals, approved project costs and announced foreign interest in a separate pipeline collection.

## Calculation and scope notes

The year-on-year percentage change is derived from the displayed rounded source inputs. The table’s rounded component periods sum to US$257.18 million, while it reports US$257.19 million cumulatively. Retain the reported cumulative figure and the US$0.01-million rounding difference. The underlying unrounded observations are unavailable here.

No five- or ten-year growth rate, comprehensive state ranking or sector/investor attribution is established by this short series. The source ends in March 2026; this record does not claim it is the latest release available in September 2026. A newer-release check is part of the research queue.

[^journey-fdi-mar2026]: [DPIIT Table 5: state-wise FDI equity inflow, October 2019–March 2026](https://www.dpiit.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/06/48c814fa57eef728bb41e26e08a75b16.pdf)

body:
# Investment in Odisha — domestic and foreign capital

## The current editorial focus

**Investment in Odisha — domestic and foreign capital, from commitment to operation.** The user replaced the standalone FDI headline track on 27 September 2026. Present values in ₹ crore or ₹ lakh crore, with stage and period beside every number. The [saved FDI series](fdi.md) remains a narrow reference, not the weekly headline.

## A supported starting point

| Measure | Period | Officially reported amount | Meaning |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 80 industrial projects described as implemented | 2025 | ₹1.75 lakh crore | Investment associated with reported implementation; cash-spend definition not established |
| 244 approved industrial projects | 2025 | ₹5.66 lakh crore | Estimated project budgets; approval does not establish expenditure |

These two values come from section 5.1.3 of the full survey's official indexed passage.[^investment-survey-full-2026] The executive summary gives less precise versions, ₹1.7 lakh crore and ₹5.6 lakh crore. Preserve both publication variants rather than treating their difference as new investment.[^investment-survey-summary-2026]

The summary also records ₹15.1 lakh crore of commitments across 275 MoUs at listed 2025 investor events, and ₹65,010 crore of state capital outlay in FY2025–26 budget estimates. These are separate coverage and status measures.[^investment-survey-summary-2026]

## What we can say

**“Odisha reports ₹1.75 lakh crore in investment across 80 industrial projects implemented in 2025.”** Attribute this to the Economic Survey and retain its implementation terminology. This is stronger evidence than an intent-only headline, but it is not an audited statewide total of cash spent or proof that every plant is operating.

The figures do not supply a domestic/foreign funding split. They are a broader industrial-investment starting point that is not restricted to the DPIIT foreign-equity series. Do not label their sum as total domestic plus foreign investment.

## Tracker design

Maintain three reader-facing views: **investment delivered**, **projects progressing**, and **future commitments**. Put an actual expenditure figure in the first view only when source scope and period support it. Keep reported implementation with its source label until commissioning or expenditure is established.

For each project capture a stable project ID, promoter, district, sector, ownership/funding origin when documented, phase, stage date, announced/approved cost, cumulative and period spending if disclosed, commissioned capacity and employment status. Unknown fields remain unknown. Match repeated announcements and expansion phases before aggregation.

Track private businesses, public-sector enterprises and government capital outlay separately. Domestic/foreign/mixed ownership and public/private ownership are different classifications. Corporate headquarters, promoter nationality or a foreign brand name do not by themselves measure how a project was financed.

Do not add MoUs, approved costs and implemented-project amounts: the same projects may appear in multiple stages. Do not add FDI flows to project costs, or cumulative capital stock to annual spending. Exclude growth/conversion rates until comparison coverage and project cohorts match. A comprehensive statewide realised investment total has not yet been established.

## Next evidence to obtain

IPICOL and Industries Department project-level implementation definitions and lists; company annual reports/exchange filings with Odisha-specific capital expenditure; commissioning evidence; Finance Accounts and budget actuals for public capital outlay; comparable five/ten-year series. Use successive releases to build evidence, not to inflate the same project's total.

- **Union Budget 2026–27:** Odisha was named alongside Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu for proposed dedicated rare-earth corridors. An April 2026 parliamentary reply said a joint working group was being constituted to develop guidelines.[^journey-rare-corridor]

- **11 August 2026:** a ministerial meeting discussed an integrated science roadmap linking the proposed corridor with marine biotechnology and other research. This release does not establish corridor commissioning or new plant output.[^weekly-rare-aug2026]

## Meaning and presentation

Show two clearly labelled layers: **established facilities** and **proposed expansion**. A simple value-chain illustration can explain mineral extraction, chemical processing and downstream manufacturing, but each stage needs its own location and evidence. IREL’s company profile places high-purity oxide refining at Aluva in Kerala; do not label the entire company value chain as located in Odisha.[^journey-irel-history]

The story opportunity is Odisha’s role in higher-value materials. Do not equate all beach-sand minerals with rare earths, or connect rare-earth projects to Odisha semiconductor projects as a confirmed supply relationship without evidence.

## What to track next

Plant-level output and capacity utilisation over time; product basis; Odisha-specific resource estimates with dates and methodology; corridor guidelines, named projects, spending and commissioning; downstream buyers and processing locations; environmental permissions and operating safeguards relevant to each facility.

The corporate page’s approximate 11,000-tonne description and the plant page’s 11,200-tpa figure have different precision. This record uses the specific plant figure and does not sum them.

# Odisha’s semiconductor journey

## The reader’s takeaway

**Two Odisha projects approved under the India Semiconductor Mission in August 2025.**

SiCSem covers silicon-carbide compound semiconductors; 3D Glass Solutions covers advanced packaging and embedded glass substrates. Approval identifies a developing pipeline, not two factories already producing commercially.[^legacy-ism]

## Milestones

- **12 August 2025 — approval:** the Union Cabinet approved SiCSem and 3D Glass Solutions projects in Odisha. SiCSem’s planned annual capacity was 60,000 wafers.[^legacy-ism]
- **19 April 2026 — groundbreaking:** the HIPS/3D Glass project at Info Valley reached its foundation-stone event. Reported project investment: **₹1,943.53 crore**. Commercial production was targeted for August 2028, with full-volume production targeted for August 2030.[^legacy-glass]
- **15 September 2026 — separate SEZ approval:** SiCSem’s proposal recorded **₹3,406.25 crore** investment and approximately **1,270 expected jobs**. These remain a proposal value and employment projection.[^legacy-sicsez]
- **18 September 2026 — wider pipeline:** MeitY reported approximately **₹23,600 crore of investment proposals**, 6,100 potential employment opportunities and an announced 870-acre Odisha Silicon Valley at Naraj. These are ecosystem proposals and an announced development.[^journey-semicon-2026]

## Meaning and presentation

Use a milestone ribbon with explicit labels: **approved → groundbreaking → construction evidence → commissioned → commercial production**. Put future targets on a visibly separate timeline. A later approval can concern an existing project rather than a new factory.

Do not add the broad September proposal total to named project estimates: overlap has not been reconciled. Do not add SiCSem’s separate approval figures as if each were additional investment. Keep planned jobs, realised headcount, installed capacity and actual output in separate fields.

The earlier [SiCSem evidence records](../evidence/s02.md) use another approval-context investment figure; its scope difference from the SEZ proposal remains unresolved. The [saved RIR update](../evidence/s11.md) remains a secondary account pending the underlying company filing. The new primary sources checked here do not establish commercial output at those facilities.

## What to track next

Project-specific construction and commissioning evidence; production-start disclosures; actual spending; employment; local supplier links; skills programmes and outcomes. Preserve the distinction between manufacturing, packaging, design and training.

title: Growth calculations and comparison rules
description: Growth calculations and comparison rules — research and reuse notes.
body:
# Growth calculations and comparison rules

Percentage change = (end value / start value − 1) × 100.

Compound annual growth rate = ((end value / start value) ** (1 / elapsed years) − 1) × 100.

For the six observations FY2019–20 through FY2024–25 there are five elapsed years. Retain unrounded values for calculations and round only for display. The [stored dataset](../references/data/industry-growth-data.json) includes the original values, source locations and interpretive caveats.

The supplied [validation tool](../tools/validate.py) recomputes both measures for all nine real sector series and ten supporting comparisons. It also checks source-reference keys and internal links. Successful arithmetic checks do not independently authenticate a source or establish comparability.

Do not add overlapping sector changes. Do not compare a current-price series to a constant-price series as if they were identical. A revised estimate supersedes an earlier vintage only when the underlying series is updated coherently. Preserve the prior record in the change history if a publication claim changes.

This is a reproducible calculation method. It is not represented as an OKF Attested Computation because this bundle does not implement an executor/receipt/attester contract.

# Search, reuse and update the knowledge base

## Read without tools

Begin at the [home index](../index.md). Browse by topic or follow links from a story to its foods, textiles, places and evidence. Every concept is plain text and can be read offline. The bibliography preserves source URLs for future checking; the external pages themselves are not all archived.

## Local search

The [search tool](../tools/search.py) searches the saved concepts and aliases without network access. From the bundle directory, use:

```sh
python3 tools/search.py "Kotpad"
python3 tools/search.py "pitha" --section food
python3 tools/search.py "growth" --section economy --limit 8
```

Search is a convenience, not an OKF requirement. It reads Markdown files directly, so edits are immediately searchable. The supplied search-index.json is a generated export for future ingestion; rebuild it with the indexing tool after changing documents.

## Add knowledge

Create a concept with a stable path, a non-empty type, title, source metadata and clearly separated fact, interpretation and research gaps. Use existing IDs where possible. Add aliases for spelling variants, and have Odia script reviewed before marking it ready. Add links to related foods, makers, places and stories. Record any actual source verification separately from authorship.

## Refresh

Check the relevant original source when a record is stale, disputed or required for a current claim. Preserve the old value in an update note, replace the complete comparable series where needed, and record the change in log.md. Rebuild the search export and run validation. A future CMS should map each feature to these stable concept IDs.

The root workspace instructions direct future research in this task to consult the KB first. No recurring update automation has been created.

title: How the maritime linked data works

body:
# How the maritime linked data works

The [JSON-LD graph](../references/data/maritime-links.jsonld) is an actual linked entity-and-claim export, alongside the OKF concept documents. It uses stable local URNs, RDF statements, Schema.org entity names and PROV source attribution. The local vocabulary and claim classes are documented within its context; they are project extensions, not part of OKF 0.2.

Each claim links a subject, predicate and object, plus evidence kind, period, source URL, supporting KB concept and limitation. Numeric observations carry value and unit; calculated observations retain inputs and formula in [the metrics dataset](../references/data/maritime-metrics.json).

## Evidence classes

- **Geographic context:** a present-day location, without equating modern borders with historical territory.
- **Archaeological finding:** reported find context, without automatically proving the carrier or route.
- **Archaeometric inference:** scientifically supported provenance with the author’s uncertainty retained.
- **Historical interpretation:** published reconstruction, not a measured sailing track.
- **Cultural commemoration:** evidence of what a ritual or institution remembers.
- **Reported statistic:** a source’s defined contemporary observation.
- **Derived statistic:** a reproducible calculation from named inputs.
- **Research lead / disputed interpretation:** searchable, but excluded from established campaign claims.

## Local queries

```sh
python3 tools/query_maritime.py China
python3 tools/query_maritime.py Paradip
python3 tools/query_maritime.py --kind archaeological_finding
python3 tools/validate_maritime.py
```

No live database or network access is required. A future website can show historical and contemporary layers separately, and reveal the source when a reader selects a connection. Graph-edge counts are counts in this research collection, not historical counts of voyages or trading partners.

## Joins that are not allowed

Do not join historical Kalinga and modern Odisha by unconditional identity. Do not treat a Chinese artefact as proof of a direct China–Odisha ship route. Do not attach Paradip throughput to every Odisha export destination. Missing state–country trade is stored as missing rather than replaced by India-level totals.

The validator checks graph integrity and arithmetic; it does not certify archaeological conclusions. This export is linked data, not an OKF Attested Computation.

title: How the statistical atlas is recorded and maintained
description: How the statistical atlas is recorded and maintained — source-linked research, scope and reuse notes.
body:
# How the statistical atlas is recorded and maintained

## One observation, one defined claim

The atlas records a number with its unit, reference period, geography, source ID, source location, definition, evidence status and caveat. Source capture notes distinguish a downloaded/inspected document, parsed HTML/PDF and indexed-only extracts. The observation date differs from the source-access date.

Publication readiness is a triage label, not editorial approval: `hold_conflict` blocks contradictory values; `needs_source_table_review` flags limited captures; `source_checked_editorial_review_pending` still needs appropriate context and final editorial selection. No human review is claimed.

## Comparison rules

Keep survey vintages, household/person denominators, age groups, sex, price bases and administrative boundaries aligned. Accounts and visits are not unique people. Capacity, registration, budget, disbursement and actual output are separate. A percentage-point change is not percentage growth. Record source-restated baselines rather than silently rewriting old values. Do not infer causal effects or significance from two point estimates.

The calculations in the structured atlas explicitly reference their inputs. They use displayed source precision; changes are descriptive, not statistical inference. Preserve flat or negative results, uncertainty and contradictions alongside compelling positive stories.

## Retrieval and updates

Use `python3 outputs/odisha-kb/tools/query_statistics.py --topic health` or `--geography Puri`; add `--query schools` for a text search. Default output shows a bounded selection; use `--limit` deliberately. Run `validate_statistics.py` after changes, alongside the bundle checks. The atlas is the maintained research record; work files are staging inputs only and must not be rerun over later edits.

Follow release cadence: monthly public accounts, quarterly banking, annual administrative reports, periodic surveys/censuses, event-based project updates and assessment-specific environmental data. Check for a successor release before calling an observation latest. Never turn a fixed historical PDF into a live measure by updating its access date.

description: Maintaining the linked visitor index — visitor index research.
body:
# Maintaining the linked visitor index

The Markdown concepts remain the canonical knowledge records. `references/data/visitor-index.json` is a local application export with stable concept-path IDs. Its fields are project extensions, not extra requirements of OKF 0.2.

## Relationships and unknowns

A food/place association is not a current venue recommendation. A regional pairing is an editorial choice. Area membership is not measured proximity. An onsite facility is linked to the named heritage site or visitor precinct; record its exact entrance separately before calculating walking routes. Unknown values are JSON null, never zero or false.

Food records retain the original source and inherited check dates. Adding them to this index is not an independent source check. New official listings record source-check scope, access date and an editorial review date. Source dates and review dates are different fields. A historical inauguration can establish infrastructure at that time; it cannot establish operation today.

## Maintenance

1. Search existing knowledge and preserve stable IDs before adding an entry.
2. Record narrow facts, source URLs and location scope. Keep editorial hooks in editorial fields.
3. Link heritage, food and facilities using the correct relationship. Add a venue-to-food link only when serving evidence exists.
4. For practical details, save provider identity, date, evidence, price units and route endpoints/mode. Do not infer availability, hygiene quality or universal accessibility.
5. Review facility listings monthly and all changing details before public recommendations. Record closures and conflicts without deleting their history.
6. Update area pages, the three catalogs and the JSON export together; validate counts and references. Run `python3 outputs/odisha-kb/tools/reindex.py`, `python3 outputs/odisha-kb/tools/validate.py` and `python3 outputs/odisha-kb/tools/validate_visitor_index.py` from the workspace.
7. Update the bundle log, summary and portable archive. No human review is recorded without a named actual reviewer.

## Retrieval

From the workspace, run `python3 outputs/odisha-kb/tools/query_visitor_index.py Cuttack` to retrieve matching areas and their linked records offline. General KB search continues to cover the underlying concepts.
